content: Magaldrate is an antacid medication commonly used for the treatment of duodenal and gastric ulcers, as well as esophagitis caused by gastroesophageal reflux. Magaldrate is available in two pharmaceutical forms: oral suspension and tablets. Pharmacologically, magaldrate is a hydroxymagnesium aluminate complex. Upon exposure to gastric acid, it is rapidly converted into magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)₂) and aluminum hydroxide (Al(OH)₃). These compounds are poorly absorbed in the gastrointestinal tract, which allows them to exert a prolonged antacid effect. Magaldrate can interact negatively with certain medications, including tetracyclines, benzodiazepines, and indomethacin, potentially reducing their efficacy. High doses or extended use of magaldrate may increase bowel movements and decrease stool consistency. In some cases, it can disrupt normal gastrointestinal function, occasionally causing either constipation or diarrhea. Magaldrate is marketed under various brand names, including Digecid Plus (Beximco Pharma, Bangladesh), Marlox Plus (Incepta Pharma, Bangladesh), Gastid (SK+F, Bangladesh), Novelta (Bangladesh), Gadral (Italy), Magaltop (Italy), Magralibi (Italy), Mylanta (Australia), and Riopan (available in Argentina, Austria, Brazil, Egypt, Germany, Italy, Mexico, Belgium, Switzerland, and Greece).
